title: Build Competitive Velocity Index and Signal Orchestration for Model Landscape
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Product and GTM lack a single operational measure that reflects how fast changes in the open model ecosystem (new model releases, quantization/FP16 support, license changes, pricing shifts, reported outages, latency/cost claims) will affect our customers and product economics. We constantly chase ad-hoc signals in Slack and spreadsheets with no standardized triage flow.

Objective: Define, build, and operationalize a Competitive Velocity Index (CVI) and signal orchestration pipeline that converts heterogeneous signals into: (a) a time-series CVI per model family, (b) per-model risk vectors (compatibility, cost delta, deployment effort), and (c) alerting rules that feed product backlog prioritization and exec dashboards.

Scope & Deliverables: 
1) Taxonomy & weighting: finalize signal taxonomy (launch, architecture changes, quantization support, price changes, licensing, security incidents, ecosystem adoption) and a scoring rubric for velocity and impact.
2) Ingest & normalization: lightweight ingestion pipeline that pulls feeds from GitHub model releases, model card scrapes, vendor blog RSS, pricing pages snapshots, Twitter filtered streams, and curated partner signals. Normalize into canonical signal events.
3) CVI computation: implement index formula (configurable weights) with historical backfill for at least 6 months for top 50 models.
4) Dashboard & alerts: product-facing dashboard in Console (per-model CVI, top contributing signals) and a webhook/email alerting system for P1/High velocity events.
5) Integration & Ops: map alerts to product prioritization flow (auto-tag PRs/epics, create Linear suggestions) and provide runbook for signal validation and false-positive triage.

Success metrics: CVI covers >= 80% of top 20 enterprise-used models, mean time from high-velocity alert to PM acknowledgement < 24h, and demonstration that 3 product decisions in Q2 are directly informed by CVI signals.

Out of scope: full automated model onboarding (will be follow-up), private customer telemetry ingestion (needs legal review).
